drivingQuestion: Does the recitation of Shema require intent, and under what conditions may laborers recite and pray while at work?
outcomeNote: Both contradictions are resolved by distinction — first paragraph versus second, wages versus meal — and a baraita is adduced in support.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוּמָּנִין — קוֹרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן וּבְרֹאשׁ הַנִּדְבָּךְ. מַה שֶּׁאֵינָן רַשָּׁאִין לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן בַּתְּפִלָּה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» The primary issue in this mishna is the requisite degree of concentration when reciting Shema. «Laborers» engaged in their work may «recite» Shema while standing «atop the tree or atop the course of stones» in a wall under construction, «which they are not permitted to do for» the Amida «prayer,» which requires intent of the heart.

segments.he: חָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְעַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת אִם לֹא עָשָׂה מַעֲשֶׂה. וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שֶׁנָּשָׂא אִשָּׁה וְקָרָא לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה. אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּלְמִידָיו: לִמַּדְתָּנוּ רַבֵּינוּ שֶׁחָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיאַת שְׁמַע? אָמַר לָהֶם אֵינִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לָכֶם לְבַטֵּל הֵימֶנִי מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
segments.en: The mishna continues: «A groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema on the first night» of his marriage, which was generally Wednesday night, «until Saturday night, if he has not taken action» and consummated the marriage, as he is preoccupied by concerns related to consummation of the marriage. The mishna relates that «there was an incident where Rabban Gamliel married a woman and recited» Shema even «the first night. His students said to him: Didn’t our teacher teach us that a groom is exempt from the recitation of Shema? He answered them:» Nevertheless, «I am not listening to you» to refrain from reciting Shema, and in so doing «preclude myself from» the acceptance of «the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven, for even one moment.»

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָאוּמָּנִין — קוֹרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן וּבְרֹאשׁ הַנִּדְבָּךְ. וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין בְּרֹאשׁ הַזַּיִת וּבְרֹאשׁ הַתְּאֵנָה. וּשְׁאָר כָּל הָאִילָנוֹת — יוֹרְדִים לְמַטָּה וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין. וּבַעַל הַבַּיִת, בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ יוֹרֵד לְמַטָּה וּמִתְפַּלֵּל, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין דַּעְתּוֹ מְיוּשֶּׁבֶת עָלָיו.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» With regard to laborers, «the Sages taught» in a Tosefta: «Laborers,» while engaged in their labor, may «recite» Shema while standing «atop the tree or atop the course of stones» in a wall under construction. «And they» may «pray atop the olive tree or the fig tree,» as those trees have many branches close together, so one could stand on them and focus properly while praying. In the case of «all the rest of the trees,» however, «they must climb down and pray.» However, «the homeowner,» who is self-employed, «in all cases,» regardless of the type of tree, «must climb down and pray, as he will be unable to focus appropriately.» Since, in contrast to the laborers, it is his prerogative to climb down and pray, the Sages did not permit him to pray atop the tree.

segments.he: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רַב מָרִי בְּרַהּ דְּבַת שְׁמוּאֵל לְרָבָא, תְּנַן: הָאוּמָּנִין קוֹרִין בְּרֹאשׁ הָאִילָן וּבְרֹאשׁ הַנִּדְבָּךְ, אַלְמָא לָא בָּעֵי כַּוָּנָה. וּרְמִינְהִי: הַקּוֹרֵא אֶת שְׁמַע צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל״, וּלְהַלָּן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״הַסְכֵּת וּשְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל״. מַה לְּהַלָּן בְּ״הַסְכֵּת״ אַף כָּאן בְּ״הַסְכֵּת״.
segments.en: «Rav Mari, son of the daughter of Shmuel, raised a contradiction before Rava: We learned» in our mishna: «Laborers may recite» Shema «atop the tree or atop the course of stones» in a wall under construction. «We see that he does not require intent,» simple recitation is sufficient. «And he raised a contradiction» from the verbal analogy taught in a baraita: «One who recites Shema must focus his heart, as it is stated: “Hear [Shema], Israel.” And below,» later in Deuteronomy, «it says: “Pay attention, and hear [shema], Israel”» (Deuteronomy 27:9). «Just as there» one must «pay attention, so too here» one must «pay attention.»

segments.he: אִשְׁתִּיק. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִידֵּי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ בְּהָא? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת — וְהוּא שֶׁבְּטֵלִין מִמְּלַאכְתָּן וְקוֹרִין.
segments.en: Rava «was silent» as he had no response. But «he said to him: Have you heard anything on this» matter? «He replied: Rav Sheshet said as follows: And this» halakha, that laborers may recite Shema atop the tree only applies «when they are idle from their work and recite» it so they can focus their hearts.

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים עוֹסְקִים בִּמְלַאכְתָּן וְקוֹרִין!
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this: «But wasn’t it taught» in a baraita that «Beit Hillel say:» Laborers «engage in their labor and recite» Shema?

segments.he: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּפֶרֶק רִאשׁוֹן, הָא בְּפֶרֶק שֵׁנִי.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: «This is not difficult. This,» which says that laborers must be idle from their labor, is referring to a case when they are reciting «the first paragraph» of Shema, «while that,» which says that they may continue to work, is in a case when they are reciting «the second paragraph.»

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַפּוֹעֲלִים שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת, קוֹרִין קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּמְבָרְכִין לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ. וְאוֹכְלִין פִּתָּן וּמְבָרְכִין לְפָנֶיהָ וּלְאַחֲרֶיהָ, וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה. אֲבָל אֵין יוֹרְדִין לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה, וְאֵין נוֹשְׂאִין כַּפֵּיהֶם.
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a Tosefta: «Laborers who were working for a homeowner» are obligated to «recite Shema and recite the blessings before it and after it; and» when they «eat their bread they» are obligated to «recite the blessing before and after it; and they» are obligated to «recite the Amida prayer. However, they do not descend before the ark» as communal prayer leaders «and» the priests among them «do not lift their hands» to recite the Priestly Blessing, so as not to be derelict in the duties they were hired to perform.

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא מֵעֵין שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה! אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא — רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, הָא — רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this: «Didn’t we learn» in a different baraita that laborers recite an abridged prayer consisting of «a microcosm of the Amida prayer» in place of the full Amida prayer? «Rav Sheshet said: This is not difficult. This» baraita obligating laborers to recite the full Amida prayer is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabban Gamliel,» as he holds that one must always recite the full eighteen blessings. «This» baraita which allows laborers to abridge their prayers is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Yehoshua,» who permits one to abridge the Amida prayer.

segments.he: אִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מַאי אִירְיָא פּוֹעֲלִים? אֲפִילּוּ כָּל אָדָם נָמֵי!
segments.en: The Gemara objects: But «if» this baraita is in accordance with the opinion of «Rabbi Yehoshua, why» did the baraita «discuss» a case involving «laborers» in particular? Rabbi Yehoshua holds that «every person may also» recite an abridged version of the Amida prayer.

segments.he: אֶלָּא אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן, בְּעוֹשִׂין בִּשְׂכָרָן. כָּאן, בְּעוֹשִׂין בִּסְעוּדָתָן.
segments.en: «Rather,» we must say that «this» baraita and «that» baraita are both in accordance with the opinion of «Rabban Gamliel, and this is not difficult: Here,» in the baraita where laborers pray the abridged version of the Amida prayer, refers to a case «where» laborers «work for their wage» beyond the meal provided by their employer; «while here,» in the baraita where laborers must pray the full Amida prayer, refers to a case «where» laborers «work» only «for their meal.»

segments.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: הַפּוֹעֲלִים שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂים מְלָאכָה אֵצֶל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת — קוֹרִין קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין. וְאוֹכְלִין פִּתָּן — וְאֵין מְבָרְכִים לְפָנֶיהָ, אֲבָל מְבָרְכִין לְאַחֲרֶיהָ שְׁתַּיִם. כֵּיצַד? בְּרָכָה רִאשׁוֹנָה כְּתִקּוּנָהּ, שְׁנִיָּה פּוֹתֵחַ בְּבִרְכַּת הָאָרֶץ וְכוֹלְלִין ״בּוֹנֵה יְרוּשָׁלָיִם״ בְּבִרְכַּת הָאָרֶץ.
segments.en: «And» indeed «it was taught» in a baraita: «Laborers who were performing labor for the homeowner recite Shema and pray; and» when they «eat their bread they do not recite a blessing beforehand» because the blessing recited before food is only an obligation by rabbinic law, «but they recite two» of the three blessings normally recited in «the blessing thereafter,» the Grace after Meals, which is an obligation by Torah law. «How so? The first blessing» is recited «in its standard» formula; «the second blessing, he begins» to recite «the blessing of the land and they include» the blessing: «Who builds Jerusalem within the blessing of the land,» at which point they conclude the Grace after Meals.

segments.he: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים — בְּעוֹשִׂין בִּשְׂכָרָן, אֲבָל עוֹשִׂין בִּסְעוּדָתָן אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת מֵיסֵב עִמָּהֶן — מְבָרְכִין כְּתִיקּוּנָהּ.
segments.en: «In what» case «is this said?» This is said «with regard to» laborers «who work for their wage, but» if they «work for their meal or if the homeowner reclined» and ate the meal «with them, they recite the blessings in their standard» formula.

moves.cueHe: האומנין קורין בראש האילן ובראש הנדבך
moves.summary: laborers may recite Shema atop a tree or a course of stones, but may not pray there

moves.cueHe: חתן פטור מקריאת שמע לילה הראשונה
moves.summary: a groom is exempt from Shema on the first night until Saturday night if he has not consummated the marriage
moves.about: Rabban Gamliel recited Shema on the first night after his marriage, though a groom is exempt

moves.cueHe: ומעשה ברבן גמליאל שנשא אשה וקרא לילה הראשונה
moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel married and recited Shema on the first night

moves.cueHe: אמרו לו תלמידיו: למדתנו רבינו שחתן פטור מקריאת שמע
moves.summary: his students press him with his own ruling that a groom is exempt
moves.about: whether Rabban Gamliel may recite Shema on his wedding night when he himself taught that a groom is exempt

moves.summary: he will not forgo the yoke of Heaven even for one moment
moves.about: he will not forgo the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven even for one moment

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן: האומנין קורין בראש האילן
moves.summary: a baraita extends the mishna: which trees they may pray atop, and that a homeowner must descend
moves.about: a baraita expanding the mishna's rule about laborers reciting and praying atop a tree

moves.cueHe: רמי ליה רב מרי ברה דבת שמואל לרבא
moves.summary: he sets the mishna, which implies no intent is needed, against a baraita requiring one to focus the heart
moves.about: whether the recitation of Shema requires intent, given that the mishna lets laborers recite atop a tree while a baraita requires focusing the heart

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: מידי שמיע לך בהא?
moves.summary: he asks Rav Mari whether he has heard a tradition on the matter
moves.about: whether Rav Mari has heard any tradition resolving the contradiction

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: הכי אמר רב ששת
moves.summary: in Rav Sheshet's name: the mishna speaks of laborers who stop their work and recite
moves.about: the mishna permits reciting atop a tree only where the laborers stop working, so intent is preserved and there is no contradiction

moves.summary: Rava is silent, having no answer
moves.about: Rava has no answer to the contradiction Rav Mari has raised and says nothing

moves.cueHe: והתניא: בית הלל אומרים עוסקים במלאכתן וקורין
moves.summary: a baraita has Beit Hillel permit reciting while working
moves.about: Beit Hillel permit laborers to recite while engaged in their work, against Rav Sheshet's requirement that they stop

moves.cueHe: לא קשיא: הא בפרק ראשון, הא בפרק שני
moves.summary: one refers to the first paragraph of Shema, the other to the second
moves.about: the requirement to stop work governs the first paragraph of Shema, Beit Hillel's permission the second

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן: הפועלים שהיו עושין מלאכה אצל בעל הבית
moves.summary: a baraita on what laborers working for a homeowner must recite and pray
moves.about: a baraita on the obligations of laborers working for a homeowner — Shema, blessings and the Amida

moves.summary: another baraita gives laborers only an abridged Amida
moves.about: another baraita has laborers recite only an abridged Amida, against the baraita requiring the full eighteen blessings

moves.cueHe: אמר רב ששת: לא קשיא, הא — רבן גמליאל, הא — רבי יהושע
moves.summary: the two baraitot follow Rabban Gamliel and R' Yehoshua respectively
moves.about: the two baraitot follow two tannaim — Rabban Gamliel, who requires the full eighteen, and R' Yehoshua, who permits an abridgement

moves.cueHe: אי רבי יהושע, מאי איריא פועלים?
moves.summary: on R' Yehoshua's view everyone may abridge, so why specify laborers
moves.about: if the abridging baraita is R' Yehoshua's, it should not have specified laborers, since he permits everyone to abridge

moves.summary: both baraitot are Rabban Gamliel's: one of laborers paid in wages, one of laborers paid in meals
moves.about: both baraitot are Rabban Gamliel's: one speaks of laborers working for wages, the other of laborers working for their meal

moves.cueHe: והתניא: הפועלים שהיו עושים מלאכה אצל בעל הבית
moves.summary: a baraita is brought that draws exactly this wages-versus-meal distinction
moves.about: a baraita distinguishing laborers who work for wages from those who work for their meal

moves.summary: its closing clause confirms the distinction: those working for their meal bless in the standard formula
moves.about: the baraita's own 'in what case is this said' clause confirms the distinction between working for wages and working for one's meal

edges.about: a baraita on the obligations of laborers working for a homeowner — Shema, blessings and the Amida

edges.cueHe: והתניא מעין שמונה עשרה!
edges.about: another baraita has laborers recite only an abridged Amida, against the baraita requiring the full eighteen blessings

edges.cueHe: והתניא
edges.about: the second baraita, prescribing an abridged Amida for laborers

edges.cueHe: אמר רב ששת: לא קשיא, הא — רבן גמליאל, הא — רבי יהושע
edges.about: the two baraitot follow two tannaim — Rabban Gamliel, who requires the full eighteen, and R' Yehoshua, who permits an abridgement

edges.cueHe: הא — רבן גמליאל
edges.about: the baraita obligating laborers in the full Amida follows Rabban Gamliel

edges.cueHe: הא — רבי יהושע
edges.about: the baraita permitting laborers an abridged Amida follows R' Yehoshua

edges.cueHe: הא — רבן גמליאל, הא — רבי יהושע
edges.about: whether one must always recite the full eighteen blessings of the Amida or may recite an abridged version

edges.cueHe: אי רבי יהושע, מאי איריא פועלים? אפילו כל אדם נמי!
edges.about: if the abridging baraita is R' Yehoshua's, it should not have specified laborers, since he permits everyone to abridge

edges.cueHe: אלא אידי ואידי רבן גמליאל, ולא קשיא: כאן, בעושין בשכרן. כאן, בעושין בסעודתן
edges.about: both baraitot are Rabban Gamliel's: one speaks of laborers working for wages, the other of laborers working for their meal

edges.cueHe: אלא אידי ואידי רבן גמליאל
edges.about: both baraitot are re-assigned to Rabban Gamliel rather than split between two tannaim

edges.cueHe: והתניא: הפועלים שהיו עושים מלאכה אצל בעל הבית
edges.about: a baraita distinguishing laborers who work for wages from those who work for their meal

edges.cueHe: במה דברים אמורים — בעושין בשכרן, אבל עושין בסעודתן
edges.about: the baraita's own 'in what case is this said' clause confirms the distinction between working for wages and working for one's meal

extras.cueHe: תנן: האומנין קורין בראש האילן ובראש הנדבך
extras.about: the mishna permitting laborers to recite Shema atop a tree

extras.cueHe: ורמינהי: הקורא את שמע צריך שיכוין את לבו
extras.about: the baraita requiring one who recites Shema to focus his heart

extras.cueHe: שנאמר: ״שמע ישראל״, ולהלן הוא אומר: ״הסכת ושמע ישראל״
extras.about: the baraita's verbal analogy brings 'Pay attention and hear, Israel' alongside 'Hear, Israel'

extras.cueHe: אמר ליה: הכי אמר רב ששת
extras.about: Rav Mari reports Rav Sheshet's qualification that the mishna speaks of laborers who stop their work
the baraita recording Beit Hillel's permission to recite while working
the second baraita, prescribing an abridged Amida for laborers

extras.cueHe: הא — רבן גמליאל, הא — רבי יהושע
extras.about: whether one must always recite the full eighteen blessings of the Amida or may recite an abridged version
